name: D7 Messaging
description: D7 Messaging lets teams send SMS, OTP, WhatsApp, and Viber messages, fetch pricing, and track delivery/status through D7's messaging APIs.

authentication.name: Bearer Token
authentication.description: Use a D7 bearer token in the Authorization header. D7 issues the token from the application login endpoint using a client_id and client_secret.

setupGuide.title: Set up your D7 bearer token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a D7 account and access to the D7 Control Panel.

steps.title: Create or open a D7 application
steps.description: In the D7 Control Panel, create an application or open an existing one so you can access its client_id and client_secret.

steps.title: Generate a bearer token
steps.description: Use the D7 authentication endpoint POST https://api.d7networks.com/auth/v1/login/application with your client_id and client_secret as form fields. The response includes access_token and token_type.

steps.title: Paste the bearer token into this connection
steps.description: Use the returned access_token as the value for this MindCloud connection. The app will send it as Authorization: Bearer <token> on API requests.

name: Dachser
description: Connect to DACHSER's REST/JSON logistics APIs for transport orders, shipment tracking, proofs of delivery, freight costs, labels, routing, SSCCs, warehouse delivery documents, delivery order statuses, incoming goods documents, and stock.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use a DACHSER API token generated or subscribed through the DACHSER API Portal. The token is sent to DACHSER as the X-API-Key header.
authentication.notes: DACHSER OpenAPI specs define API key auth in the `X-API-Key` header. The public token generator produces 10-day test tokens and states that generated tokens are not suitable for production or for transportorder test subscriptions.

description: Manage Databricks account and workspace resources through official Databricks REST APIs using OAuth 2.0 service-principal credentials.

setupGuide.title: Connect Databricks
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Databricks service principal with the permissions required for the account and workspace APIs you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Open the Databricks account console
steps.description: Sign in to the Databricks account console for the Databricks account that owns the workspace you want to connect.

steps.title: Create or choose a service principal
steps.description: In the Databricks account console, create a service principal or open an existing one for this MindCloud connection.

steps.title: Generate an OAuth secret
steps.description: Create a client secret for the service principal and copy the Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Copy the account ID and workspace URL
steps.description: Copy the Databricks account ID from the account console and the target workspace URL, for example https://dbc-a1b2345c-d6e7.cloud.databricks.com.

steps.title: Grant the service principal access
steps.description: Assign the Databricks account-level and workspace-level permissions required for the APIs you want to use from MindCloud.

steps.title: Enter the credentials in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the Workspace URL, Account ID, Client ID, and Client Secret into this connection and save it.

actions.name: Create Cluster
actions.description: Creates a new cluster in the Databricks workspace.

arguments.name: Apply Policy Default Values
arguments.description:
When set to true, fixed and default values from the policy will be used for fields that are omitted.
When set to false, only fixed values from the policy will be applied.

arguments.name: Max Workers
arguments.description:
The maximum number of workers to which the cluster can scale up when overloaded.
Note that `max_workers` must be strictly greater than `min_workers`.

arguments.name: Min Workers

arguments.name: Availability
arguments.description:

Note: If `first_on_demand` is zero, this availability type will be used for the entire cluster.

arguments.name: Ebs Volume Count
arguments.description:
The number of volumes launched for each instance. Users can choose up to 10 volumes.
This feature is only enabled for supported node types. Legacy node types cannot specify
custom EBS volumes.
For node types with no instance store, at least one EBS volume needs to be specified;
otherwise, cluster creation will fail.

These EBS volumes will be mounted at `/ebs0`, `/ebs1`, and etc.
Instance store volumes will be mounted at `/local_disk0`, `/local_disk1`, and etc.

If EBS volumes are attached, Databricks will configure Spark to use only the EBS volumes for
scratch storage because heterogenously sized scratch devices can lead to inefficient disk
utilization. If no EBS volumes are attached, Databricks will configure Spark to use instance
store volumes.

Please note that if EBS volumes are specified, then the Spark configuration `spark.local.dir`
will be overridden.

arguments.description: If using gp3 volumes, what IOPS to use for the disk. If this is not set, the maximum performance of a gp2 volume with the same volume size will be used.

arguments.name: Ebs Volume Size
arguments.description:

SSD, this value must be within the range 100 - 4096. For throughput optimized HDD,
this value must be within the range 500 - 4096.

arguments.name: Ebs Volume Throughput
arguments.description: If using gp3 volumes, what throughput to use for the disk. If this is not set, the maximum performance of a gp2 volume with the same volume size will be used.

arguments.name: Ebs Volume Type
arguments.description:

arguments.name: First On Demand
arguments.description:
The first `first_on_demand` nodes of the cluster will be placed on on-demand instances.
If this value is greater than 0, the cluster driver node in particular will be placed on an
on-demand instance. If this value is greater than or equal to the current cluster size, all
nodes will be placed on on-demand instances. If this value is less than the current cluster
size, `first_on_demand` nodes will be placed on on-demand instances and the remainder will
be placed on `availability` instances. Note that this value does not affect

ommitted, nodes will be placed on instances without an IAM instance profile. The instance

administrator.

on-demand price.
For example, if this field is set to 50, and the cluster needs a new `r3.xlarge` spot
instance, then the bid price is half of the price of
on-demand `r3.xlarge` instances. Similarly, if this field is set to 200, the bid price is twice

percentage matches this field will be considered.

and will retry placement in a different AZ if there is not enough capacity.

from a cluster.

The following modes can only be used when `kind = CLASSIC_PREVIEW`.

* `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER_STANDARD`: This mode provides a way that doesnât have UC nor passthrough enabled.

arguments.name: On Streaming Backlog Exceeded
arguments.description:

Streaming backlog thresholds can be set in the `health` field using the following metrics: `STREAMING_BACKLOG_BYTES`, `STREAMING_BACKLOG_RECORDS`, `STREAMING_BACKLOG_SECONDS`, or `STREAMING_BACKLOG_FILES`.

arguments.name: Max Concurrent Runs
arguments.description:
An optional maximum allowed number of concurrent runs of the job.
Set this value if you want to be able to execute multiple runs of the same job concurrently.
This is useful for example if you trigger your job on a frequent schedule and want to allow consecutive runs to overlap with each other, or if you want to trigger multiple runs which differ by their input parameters.
This setting affects only new runs. For example, suppose the jobâs concurrency is 4 and there are 4 concurrent active runs. Then setting the concurrency to 3 wonât kill any of the active runs.
However, from then on, new runs are skipped unless there are fewer than 3 active runs.
This value cannot exceed 1000. Setting this value to `0` causes all new runs to be skipped.

The performance mode on the job or pipeline should map to a performance setting that is passed to Cluster Manager

arguments.name: User Name
arguments.description: The email of an active workspace user. Non-admin users can only set this field to their own email.

arguments.name: Metric
arguments.description:
Specifies the health metric that is being evaluated for a particular health rule.

* `RUN_DURATION_SECONDS`: Expected total time for a run in seconds.
* `STREAMING_BACKLOG_BYTES`: An estimate of the maximum bytes of data waiting to be consumed across all streams. This metric is in Public Preview.
* `STREAMING_BACKLOG_RECORDS`: An estimate of the maximum offset lag across all streams. This metric is in Public Preview.
* `STREAMING_BACKLOG_SECONDS`: An estimate of the maximum consumer delay across all streams. This metric is in Public Preview.
* `STREAMING_BACKLOG_FILES`: An estimate of the maximum number of outstanding files across all streams. This metric is in Public Preview.

arguments.name: Op
arguments.description: Specifies the operator used to compare the health metric value with the specified threshold.

arguments.name: Value
arguments.description: Specifies the threshold value that the health metric should obey to satisfy the health rule.

arguments.name: Quartz Cron Expression
arguments.description: A Cron expression using Quartz syntax that describes the schedule for a job. See [Cron Trigger](http://www.quartz-scheduler.org/documentation/quartz-2.3.0/tutorials/crontrigger.html) for details. This field is required.

arguments.name: Timezone Id
arguments.description: A Java timezone ID. The schedule for a job is resolved with respect to this timezone. See [Java TimeZone](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/7/docs/api/java/util/TimeZone.html) for details. This field is required.

arguments.name: Job Cluster Key
arguments.description:
A unique name for the job cluster. This field is required and must be unique within the job.
`JobTaskSettings` may refer to this field to determine which cluster to launch for the task execution.

arguments.name: Tags
arguments.description: A map of tags associated with the job. These are forwarded to the cluster as cluster tags for jobs clusters, and are subject to the same limitations as cluster tags. A maximum of 25 tags can be added to the job.

arguments.name: New Cluster
arguments.description: Contains a snapshot of the latest user specified settings that were used to create/edit the cluster.

arguments.name: Tasks
arguments.description:
A list of task specifications to be executed by this job.
It supports up to 1000 elements in write endpoints (:method:jobs/create, :method:jobs/reset, :method:jobs/update, :method:jobs/submit).
Read endpoints return only 100 tasks. If more than 100 tasks are available, you can paginate through them using :method:jobs/get. Use the `next_page_token` field at the object root to determine if more results are available.

arguments.name: Apply Policy Default Values
arguments.description: When set to true, fixed and default values from the policy will be used for fields that are omitted. When set to false, only fixed values from the policy will be applied.

arguments.name: Timeout Seconds
arguments.description: An optional timeout applied to each run of this job. A value of `0` means no timeout.

arguments.name: Max Workers
arguments.description:
The maximum number of workers to which the cluster can scale up when overloaded.
Note that `max_workers` must be strictly greater than `min_workers`.

arguments.name: Min Workers
arguments.description:
The minimum number of workers to which the cluster can scale down when underutilized.
It is also the initial number of workers the cluster will have after creation.

arguments.name: Autotermination Minutes
arguments.description:
Automatically terminates the cluster after it is inactive for this time in minutes. If not set,
this cluster will not be automatically terminated. If specified, the threshold must be between
10 and 10000 minutes.
Users can also set this value to 0 to explicitly disable automatic termination.

arguments.name: Aws Attributes
arguments.description: Attributes set during cluster creation which are related to Amazon Web Services.

arguments.name: Availability
arguments.description:
Availability type used for all subsequent nodes past the `first_on_demand` ones.

Note: If `first_on_demand` is zero, this availability type will be used for the entire cluster.

arguments.name: Ebs Volume Count
arguments.description:
The number of volumes launched for each instance. Users can choose up to 10 volumes.
This feature is only enabled for supported node types. Legacy node types cannot specify
custom EBS volumes.
For node types with no instance store, at least one EBS volume needs to be specified;
otherwise, cluster creation will fail.

These EBS volumes will be mounted at `/ebs0`, `/ebs1`, and etc.
Instance store volumes will be mounted at `/local_disk0`, `/local_disk1`, and etc.

If EBS volumes are attached, Databricks will configure Spark to use only the EBS volumes for
scratch storage because heterogenously sized scratch devices can lead to inefficient disk
utilization. If no EBS volumes are attached, Databricks will configure Spark to use instance
store volumes.

Please note that if EBS volumes are specified, then the Spark configuration `spark.local.dir`
will be overridden.

arguments.name: On Duration Warning Threshold Exceeded
arguments.description: An optional list of system notification IDs to call when the duration of a run exceeds the threshold specified for the `RUN_DURATION_SECONDS` metric in the `health` field. A maximum of 3 destinations can be specified for the `on_duration_warning_threshold_exceeded` property.

arguments.name: Ebs Volume Iops
arguments.description: If using gp3 volumes, what IOPS to use for the disk. If this is not set, the maximum performance of a gp2 volume with the same volume size will be used.

arguments.name: On Failure
arguments.description: An optional list of system notification IDs to call when the run fails. A maximum of 3 destinations can be specified for the `on_failure` property.

arguments.name: Ebs Volume Size
arguments.description:
The size of each EBS volume (in GiB) launched for each instance. For general purpose
SSD, this value must be within the range 100 - 4096. For throughput optimized HDD,
this value must be within the range 500 - 4096.

arguments.name: On Start
arguments.description: An optional list of system notification IDs to call when the run starts. A maximum of 3 destinations can be specified for the `on_start` property.

arguments.name: Ebs Volume Throughput
arguments.description: If using gp3 volumes, what throughput to use for the disk. If this is not set, the maximum performance of a gp2 volume with the same volume size will be used.

arguments.name: On Streaming Backlog Exceeded
arguments.description:
An optional list of system notification IDs to call when any streaming backlog thresholds are exceeded for any stream.
Streaming backlog thresholds can be set in the `health` field using the following metrics: `STREAMING_BACKLOG_BYTES`, `STREAMING_BACKLOG_RECORDS`, `STREAMING_BACKLOG_SECONDS`, or `STREAMING_BACKLOG_FILES`.
Alerting is based on the 10-minute average of these metrics. If the issue persists, notifications are resent every 30 minutes.
A maximum of 3 destinations can be specified for the `on_streaming_backlog_exceeded` property.

arguments.name: Ebs Volume Type
arguments.description:
All EBS volume types that Databricks supports.
See https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/details/ for details.

arguments.name: On Success
arguments.description: An optional list of system notification IDs to call when the run completes successfully. A maximum of 3 destinations can be specified for the `on_success` property.

arguments.name: First On Demand
arguments.description:
The first `first_on_demand` nodes of the cluster will be placed on on-demand instances.
If this value is greater than 0, the cluster driver node in particular will be placed on an
on-demand instance. If this value is greater than or equal to the current cluster size, all
nodes will be placed on on-demand instances. If this value is less than the current cluster
size, `first_on_demand` nodes will be placed on on-demand instances and the remainder will
be placed on `availability` instances. Note that this value does not affect
cluster size and cannot currently be mutated over the lifetime of a cluster.

arguments.name: Instance Profile Arn
arguments.description:
Nodes for this cluster will only be placed on AWS instances with this instance profile. If
ommitted, nodes will be placed on instances without an IAM instance profile. The instance
profile must have previously been added to the Databricks environment by an account
administrator.

This feature may only be available to certain customer plans.

arguments.name: Spot Bid Price Percent
arguments.description:
The bid price for AWS spot instances, as a percentage of the corresponding instance type's
on-demand price.
For example, if this field is set to 50, and the cluster needs a new `r3.xlarge` spot
instance, then the bid price is half of the price of
on-demand `r3.xlarge` instances. Similarly, if this field is set to 200, the bid price is twice
the price of on-demand `r3.xlarge` instances. If not specified, the default value is 100.
When spot instances are requested for this cluster, only spot instances whose bid price
percentage matches this field will be considered.
Note that, for safety, we enforce this field to be no more than 10000.

arguments.name: Zone Id
arguments.description:
Identifier for the availability zone/datacenter in which the cluster resides.
This string will be of a form like "us-west-2a". The provided availability
zone must be in the same region as the Databricks deployment. For example, "us-west-2a"
is not a valid zone id if the Databricks deployment resides in the "us-east-1" region.
This is an optional field at cluster creation, and if not specified, the zone "auto" will be used.
If the zone specified is "auto", will try to place cluster in a zone with high availability,
and will retry placement in a different AZ if there is not enough capacity.

The list of available zones as well as the default value can be found by using the
`List Zones` method.

* `STREAMING_BACKLOG_FILES`: An estimate of the maximum number of outstanding files across all streams. This metric is in Public Preview.

arguments.name: Op
arguments.description: Specifies the operator used to compare the health metric value with the specified threshold.

arguments.name: Value
arguments.description: Specifies the threshold value that the health metric should obey to satisfy the health rule.

arguments.name: Quartz Cron Expression
arguments.description: A Cron expression using Quartz syntax that describes the schedule for a job. See [Cron Trigger](http://www.quartz-scheduler.org/documentation/quartz-2.3.0/tutorials/crontrigger.html) for details. This field is required.

arguments.name: Timezone Id
arguments.description: A Java timezone ID. The schedule for a job is resolved with respect to this timezone. See [Java TimeZone](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/7/docs/api/java/util/TimeZone.html) for details. This field is required.

arguments.name: Job Cluster Key
arguments.description:
A unique name for the job cluster. This field is required and must be unique within the job.
`JobTaskSettings` may refer to this field to determine which cluster to launch for the task execution.

arguments.name: Tags
arguments.description: A map of tags associated with the job. These are forwarded to the cluster as cluster tags for jobs clusters, and are subject to the same limitations as cluster tags. A maximum of 25 tags can be added to the job.

arguments.name: New Cluster
arguments.description: Contains a snapshot of the latest user specified settings that were used to create/edit the cluster.

arguments.name: Tasks
arguments.description:
A list of task specifications to be executed by this job.
It supports up to 1000 elements in write endpoints (:method:jobs/create, :method:jobs/reset, :method:jobs/update, :method:jobs/submit).
Read endpoints return only 100 tasks. If more than 100 tasks are available, you can paginate through them using :method:jobs/get. Use the `next_page_token` field at the object root to determine if more results are available.

arguments.name: Apply Policy Default Values
arguments.description: When set to true, fixed and default values from the policy will be used for fields that are omitted. When set to false, only fixed values from the policy will be applied.

arguments.name: Timeout Seconds
arguments.description: An optional timeout applied to each run of this job. A value of `0` means no timeout.

arguments.name: Max Workers
arguments.description:
The maximum number of workers to which the cluster can scale up when overloaded.
Note that `max_workers` must be strictly greater than `min_workers`.

arguments.name: Min Workers
arguments.description:
The minimum number of workers to which the cluster can scale down when underutilized.
It is also the initial number of workers the cluster will have after creation.

arguments.name: Autotermination Minutes
arguments.description:
Automatically terminates the cluster after it is inactive for this time in minutes. If not set,
this cluster will not be automatically terminated. If specified, the threshold must be between
10 and 10000 minutes.
Users can also set this value to 0 to explicitly disable automatic termination.

arguments.name: Aws Attributes
arguments.description: Attributes set during cluster creation which are related to Amazon Web Services.

arguments.name: Availability
arguments.description:
Availability type used for all subsequent nodes past the `first_on_demand` ones.

Note: If `first_on_demand` is zero, this availability type will be used for the entire cluster.

arguments.name: Ebs Volume Count
arguments.description:
The number of volumes launched for each instance. Users can choose up to 10 volumes.
This feature is only enabled for supported node types. Legacy node types cannot specify
custom EBS volumes.
For node types with no instance store, at least one EBS volume needs to be specified;
otherwise, cluster creation will fail.

These EBS volumes will be mounted at `/ebs0`, `/ebs1`, and etc.
Instance store volumes will be mounted at `/local_disk0`, `/local_disk1`, and etc.

If EBS volumes are attached, Databricks will configure Spark to use only the EBS volumes for
scratch storage because heterogenously sized scratch devices can lead to inefficient disk
utilization. If no EBS volumes are attached, Databricks will configure Spark to use instance
store volumes.

Please note that if EBS volumes are specified, then the Spark configuration `spark.local.dir`
will be overridden.

arguments.name: On Duration Warning Threshold Exceeded
arguments.description: An optional list of system notification IDs to call when the duration of a run exceeds the threshold specified for the `RUN_DURATION_SECONDS` metric in the `health` field. A maximum of 3 destinations can be specified for the `on_duration_warning_threshold_exceeded` property.

arguments.name: Ebs Volume Iops
arguments.description: If using gp3 volumes, what IOPS to use for the disk. If this is not set, the maximum performance of a gp2 volume with the same volume size will be used.

arguments.name: On Failure
arguments.description: An optional list of system notification IDs to call when the run fails. A maximum of 3 destinations can be specified for the `on_failure` property.

arguments.name: Ebs Volume Size
arguments.description:
The size of each EBS volume (in GiB) launched for each instance. For general purpose
SSD, this value must be within the range 100 - 4096. For throughput optimized HDD,
this value must be within the range 500 - 4096.

arguments.name: On Start
arguments.description: An optional list of system notification IDs to call when the run starts. A maximum of 3 destinations can be specified for the `on_start` property.

arguments.name: Ebs Volume Throughput
arguments.description: If using gp3 volumes, what throughput to use for the disk. If this is not set, the maximum performance of a gp2 volume with the same volume size will be used.

arguments.name: On Streaming Backlog Exceeded
arguments.description:
An optional list of system notification IDs to call when any streaming backlog thresholds are exceeded for any stream.
Streaming backlog thresholds can be set in the `health` field using the following metrics: `STREAMING_BACKLOG_BYTES`, `STREAMING_BACKLOG_RECORDS`, `STREAMING_BACKLOG_SECONDS`, or `STREAMING_BACKLOG_FILES`.
Alerting is based on the 10-minute average of these metrics. If the issue persists, notifications are resent every 30 minutes.
A maximum of 3 destinations can be specified for the `on_streaming_backlog_exceeded` property.

arguments.name: Ebs Volume Type
arguments.description:
All EBS volume types that Databricks supports.
See https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/details/ for details.

arguments.name: On Success
arguments.description: An optional list of system notification IDs to call when the run completes successfully. A maximum of 3 destinations can be specified for the `on_success` property.

arguments.name: First On Demand
arguments.description:
The first `first_on_demand` nodes of the cluster will be placed on on-demand instances.
If this value is greater than 0, the cluster driver node in particular will be placed on an
on-demand instance. If this value is greater than or equal to the current cluster size, all
nodes will be placed on on-demand instances. If this value is less than the current cluster
size, `first_on_demand` nodes will be placed on on-demand instances and the remainder will
be placed on `availability` instances. Note that this value does not affect
cluster size and cannot currently be mutated over the lifetime of a cluster.

arguments.name: Instance Profile Arn
arguments.description:
Nodes for this cluster will only be placed on AWS instances with this instance profile. If
ommitted, nodes will be placed on instances without an IAM instance profile. The instance
profile must have previously been added to the Databricks environment by an account
administrator.

This feature may only be available to certain customer plans.

arguments.name: Spot Bid Price Percent
arguments.description:
The bid price for AWS spot instances, as a percentage of the corresponding instance type's
on-demand price.
For example, if this field is set to 50, and the cluster needs a new `r3.xlarge` spot
instance, then the bid price is half of the price of
on-demand `r3.xlarge` instances. Similarly, if this field is set to 200, the bid price is twice
the price of on-demand `r3.xlarge` instances. If not specified, the default value is 100.
When spot instances are requested for this cluster, only spot instances whose bid price
percentage matches this field will be considered.
Note that, for safety, we enforce this field to be no more than 10000.

arguments.name: Zone Id
arguments.description:
Identifier for the availability zone/datacenter in which the cluster resides.
This string will be of a form like "us-west-2a". The provided availability
zone must be in the same region as the Databricks deployment. For example, "us-west-2a"
is not a valid zone id if the Databricks deployment resides in the "us-east-1" region.
This is an optional field at cluster creation, and if not specified, the zone "auto" will be used.
If the zone specified is "auto", will try to place cluster in a zone with high availability,
and will retry placement in a different AZ if there is not enough capacity.

The list of available zones as well as the default value can be found by using the
`List Zones` method.

Data security mode decides what data governance model to use when accessing data
from a cluster.

The following modes can only be used when `kind = CLASSIC_PREVIEW`.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_AUTO`: Databricks will choose the most appropriate access mode depending on your compute configuration.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_STANDARD`: Alias for `USER_ISOLATION`.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_DEDICATED`: Alias for `SINGLE_USER`.

The following modes can be used regardless of `kind`.
* `NONE`: No security isolation for multiple users sharing the cluster. Data governance features are not available in this mode.
* `SINGLE_USER`: A secure cluster that can only be exclusively used by a single user specified in `single_user_name`. Most programming languages, cluster features and data governance features are available in this mode.
* `USER_ISOLATION`: A secure cluster that can be shared by multiple users. Cluster users are fully isolated so that they cannot see each other's data and credentials. Most data governance features are supported in this mode. But programming languages and cluster features might be limited.

will be removed for future Databricks Runtime versions:

* `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on standard clusters.

Data security mode decides what data governance model to use when accessing data
from a cluster.

The following modes can only be used when `kind = CLASSIC_PREVIEW`.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_AUTO`: Databricks will choose the most appropriate access mode depending on your compute configuration.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_STANDARD`: Alias for `USER_ISOLATION`.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_DEDICATED`: Alias for `SINGLE_USER`.

The following modes can be used regardless of `kind`.
* `NONE`: No security isolation for multiple users sharing the cluster. Data governance features are not available in this mode.
* `SINGLE_USER`: A secure cluster that can only be exclusively used by a single user specified in `single_user_name`. Most programming languages, cluster features and data governance features are available in this mode.
* `USER_ISOLATION`: A secure cluster that can be shared by multiple users. Cluster users are fully isolated so that they cannot see each other's data and credentials. Most data governance features are supported in this mode. But programming languages and cluster features might be limited.

The following modes are deprecated starting with Databricks Runtime 15.0 and
will be removed for future Databricks Runtime versions:

* `LEGACY_TABLE_ACL`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Table ACL clusters.
* `LEGACY_PASSTHROUGH`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on high concurrency clusters.
* `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on standard clusters.
* `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER_STANDARD`: This mode provides a way that doesnât have UC nor passthrough enabled.

* `USER_ISOLATION`: A secure cluster that can be shared by multiple users. Cluster users are fully isolated so that they cannot see each other's data and credentials. Most data governance features are supported in this mode. But programming languages and cluster features might be limited.

* `LEGACY_PASSTHROUGH`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on high concurrency clusters.
* `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on standard clusters.
* `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER_STANDARD`: This mode provides a way that doesnât have UC nor passthrough enabled.

Data security mode decides what data governance model to use when accessing data
from a cluster.

The following modes can only be used when `kind = CLASSIC_PREVIEW`.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_AUTO`: Databricks will choose the most appropriate access mode depending on your compute configuration.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_STANDARD`: Alias for `USER_ISOLATION`.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_DEDICATED`: Alias for `SINGLE_USER`.

The following modes can be used regardless of `kind`.
* `NONE`: No security isolation for multiple users sharing the cluster. Data governance features are not available in this mode.
* `SINGLE_USER`: A secure cluster that can only be exclusively used by a single user specified in `single_user_name`. Most programming languages, cluster features and data governance features are available in this mode.
* `USER_ISOLATION`: A secure cluster that can be shared by multiple users. Cluster users are fully isolated so that they cannot see each other's data and credentials. Most data governance features are supported in this mode. But programming languages and cluster features might be limited.

The following modes are deprecated starting with Databricks Runtime 15.0 and
will be removed for future Databricks Runtime versions:

* `LEGACY_TABLE_ACL`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Table ACL clusters.
* `LEGACY_PASSTHROUGH`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on high concurrency clusters.
* `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on standard clusters.
* `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER_STANDARD`: This mode provides a way that doesnât have UC nor passthrough enabled.

Data security mode decides what data governance model to use when accessing data
from a cluster.

The following modes can only be used when `kind = CLASSIC_PREVIEW`.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_AUTO`: Databricks will choose the most appropriate access mode depending on your compute configuration.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_STANDARD`: Alias for `USER_ISOLATION`.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_DEDICATED`: Alias for `SINGLE_USER`.

The following modes can be used regardless of `kind`.
* `NONE`: No security isolation for multiple users sharing the cluster. Data governance features are not available in this mode.
* `SINGLE_USER`: A secure cluster that can only be exclusively used by a single user specified in `single_user_name`. Most programming languages, cluster features and data governance features are available in this mode.
* `USER_ISOLATION`: A secure cluster that can be shared by multiple users. Cluster users are fully isolated so that they cannot see each other's data and credentials. Most data governance features are supported in this mode. But programming languages and cluster features might be limited.

The following modes are deprecated starting with Databricks Runtime 15.0 and
will be removed for future Databricks Runtime versions:

* `LEGACY_TABLE_ACL`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Table ACL clusters.
* `LEGACY_PASSTHROUGH`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on high concurrency clusters.
* `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on standard clusters.
* `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER_STANDARD`: This mode provides a way that doesnât have UC nor passthrough enabled.

Data security mode decides what data governance model to use when accessing data
from a cluster.

The following modes can only be used when `kind = CLASSIC_PREVIEW`.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_AUTO`: Databricks will choose the most appropriate access mode depending on your compute configuration.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_STANDARD`: Alias for `USER_ISOLATION`.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_DEDICATED`: Alias for `SINGLE_USER`.

The following modes can be used regardless of `kind`.
* `NONE`: No security isolation for multiple users sharing the cluster. Data governance features are not available in this mode.
* `SINGLE_USER`: A secure cluster that can only be exclusively used by a single user specified in `single_user_name`. Most programming languages, cluster features and data governance features are available in this mode.
* `USER_ISOLATION`: A secure cluster that can be shared by multiple users. Cluster users are fully isolated so that they cannot see each other's data and credentials. Most data governance features are supported in this mode. But programming languages and cluster features might be limited.

The following modes are deprecated starting with Databricks Runtime 15.0 and
will be removed for future Databricks Runtime versions:

* `LEGACY_TABLE_ACL`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Table ACL clusters.
* `LEGACY_PASSTHROUGH`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on high concurrency clusters.
* `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on standard clusters.
* `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER_STANDARD`: This mode provides a way that doesnât have UC nor passthrough enabled.

arguments.name: Data Security Mode
arguments.description:
Data security mode decides what data governance model to use when accessing data
from a cluster.

The following modes can only be used when `kind = CLASSIC_PREVIEW`.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_AUTO`: Databricks will choose the most appropriate access mode depending on your compute configuration.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_STANDARD`: Alias for `USER_ISOLATION`.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_DEDICATED`: Alias for `SINGLE_USER`.

The following modes can be used regardless of `kind`.
* `NONE`: No security isolation for multiple users sharing the cluster. Data governance features are not available in this mode.
* `SINGLE_USER`: A secure cluster that can only be exclusively used by a single user specified in `single_user_name`. Most programming languages, cluster features and data governance features are available in this mode.
* `USER_ISOLATION`: A secure cluster that can be shared by multiple users. Cluster users are fully isolated so that they cannot see each other's data and credentials. Most data governance features are supported in this mode. But programming languages and cluster features might be limited.

The following modes are deprecated starting with Databricks Runtime 15.0 and
will be removed for future Databricks Runtime versions:

* `LEGACY_TABLE_ACL`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Table ACL clusters.
* `LEGACY_PASSTHROUGH`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on high concurrency clusters.
* `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on standard clusters.
* `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER_STANDARD`: This mode provides a way that doesnât have UC nor passthrough enabled.

arguments.name: Kind
arguments.description:
The kind of compute described by this compute specification.

Depending on `kind`, different validations and default values will be applied.

Clusters with `kind = CLASSIC_PREVIEW` support the following fields, whereas clusters with no specified `kind` do not.
* [is_single_node](/api/workspace/clusters/create#is_single_node)
* [use_ml_runtime](/api/workspace/clusters/create#use_ml_runtime)
* [data_security_mode](/api/workspace/clusters/create#data_security_mode) set to `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_AUTO`, `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_DEDICATED`, or `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_STANDARD`

By using the [simple form](https://docs.databricks.com/compute/simple-form.html), your clusters are automatically using `kind = CLASSIC_PREVIEW`.

arguments.name: Node Type Id
arguments.description:
This field encodes, through a single value, the resources available to each of
the Spark nodes in this cluster. For example, the Spark nodes can be provisioned
and optimized for memory or compute intensive workloads. A list of available node
types can be retrieved by using the :method:clusters/listNodeTypes API call.

arguments.name: Num Workers
arguments.description:
Number of worker nodes that this cluster should have. A cluster has one Spark Driver
and `num_workers` Executors for a total of `num_workers` + 1 Spark nodes.

Note: When reading the properties of a cluster, this field reflects the desired number
of workers rather than the actual current number of workers. For instance, if a cluster
is resized from 5 to 10 workers, this field will immediately be updated to reflect
the target size of 10 workers, whereas the workers listed in `spark_info` will gradually
increase from 5 to 10 as the new nodes are provisioned.

Users can also pass in a string of extra JVM options to the driver and the executors via
`spark.driver.extraJavaOptions` and `spark.executor.extraJavaOptions` respectively.

arguments.name: Spark Env Vars
arguments.description:
An object containing a set of optional, user-specified environment variable key-value pairs.
Please note that key-value pair of the form (X,Y) will be exported as is (i.e.,
`export X='Y'`) while launching the driver and workers.

In order to specify an additional set of `SPARK_DAEMON_JAVA_OPTS`, we recommend appending
them to `$SPARK_DAEMON_JAVA_OPTS` as shown in the example below. This ensures that all
default databricks managed environmental variables are included as well.

Example Spark environment variables:
`{"SPARK_WORKER_MEMORY": "28000m", "SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS": "/local_disk0"}` or
`{"SPARK_DAEMON_JAVA_OPTS": "$SPARK_DAEMON_JAVA_OPTS -Dspark.shuffle.service.enabled=true"}`

arguments.description:
Used to specify which cluster attributes and size fields to update. See https://google.aip.dev/161 for more details.

The field mask must be a single string, with multiple fields separated by commas (no spaces). The field path is relative to the resource object, using a dot (`.`) to navigate sub-fields (e.g., `author.given_name`). Specification of elements in sequence or map fields is not allowed, as only the entire collection field can be specified. Field names must exactly match the resource field names.

A field mask of `*` indicates full replacement. Itâs recommended to always explicitly list the fields being updated and avoid using `*` wildcards, as it can lead to unintended results if the API changes in the future.

arguments.name: Autotermination Minutes
arguments.description:
Automatically terminates the cluster after it is inactive for this time in minutes. If not set,
this cluster will not be automatically terminated. If specified, the threshold must be between
10 and 10000 minutes.
Users can also set this value to 0 to explicitly disable automatic termination.

arguments.name: Cluster Name

If not specified at creation, the cluster name will be an empty string.
For job clusters, the cluster name is automatically set based on the job and job run IDs.

arguments.name: Custom Tags
arguments.description:
Additional tags for cluster resources. Databricks will tag all cluster resources (e.g., AWS
instances and EBS volumes) with these tags in addition to `default_tags`. Notes:

- Currently, Databricks allows at most 45 custom tags

- Clusters can only reuse cloud resources if the resources' tags are a subset of the cluster tags

arguments.name: Data Security Mode
arguments.description:
Data security mode decides what data governance model to use when accessing data
from a cluster.

The following modes can only be used when `kind = CLASSIC_PREVIEW`.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_AUTO`: Databricks will choose the most appropriate access mode depending on your compute configuration.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_STANDARD`: Alias for `USER_ISOLATION`.
* `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_DEDICATED`: Alias for `SINGLE_USER`.

The following modes can be used regardless of `kind`.
* `NONE`: No security isolation for multiple users sharing the cluster. Data governance features are not available in this mode.
* `SINGLE_USER`: A secure cluster that can only be exclusively used by a single user specified in `single_user_name`. Most programming languages, cluster features and data governance features are available in this mode.
* `USER_ISOLATION`: A secure cluster that can be shared by multiple users. Cluster users are fully isolated so that they cannot see each other's data and credentials. Most data governance features are supported in this mode. But programming languages and cluster features might be limited.

The following modes are deprecated starting with Databricks Runtime 15.0 and
will be removed for future Databricks Runtime versions:

* `LEGACY_TABLE_ACL`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Table ACL clusters.
* `LEGACY_PASSTHROUGH`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on high concurrency clusters.
* `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER`: This mode is for users migrating from legacy Passthrough on standard clusters.
* `LEGACY_SINGLE_USER_STANDARD`: This mode provides a way that doesnât have UC nor passthrough enabled.

arguments.description:

The pool cluster uses the instance pool with id (instance_pool_id) if the driver pool is not
assigned.

arguments.name: Driver Node Type Id
arguments.description:

Note that this field is optional; if unset, the driver node type will be set as the same value
as `node_type_id` defined above.

This field, along with node_type_id, should not be set if virtual_cluster_size is set.
If both driver_node_type_id, node_type_id, and virtual_cluster_size are specified, driver_node_type_id and node_type_id take precedence.

arguments.description:

space when its Spark workers are running low on disk space.  This feature requires specific AWS

The scripts are executed sequentially in the order provided.

arguments.name: Kind
arguments.description:
The kind of compute described by this compute specification.

Depending on `kind`, different validations and default values will be applied.

Clusters with `kind = CLASSIC_PREVIEW` support the following fields, whereas clusters with no specified `kind` do not.
* [is_single_node](/api/workspace/clusters/create#is_single_node)
* [use_ml_runtime](/api/workspace/clusters/create#use_ml_runtime)
* [data_security_mode](/api/workspace/clusters/create#data_security_mode) set to `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_AUTO`, `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_DEDICATED`, or `DATA_SECURITY_MODE_STANDARD`

By using the [simple form](https://docs.databricks.com/compute/simple-form.html), your clusters are automatically using `kind = CLASSIC_PREVIEW`.

arguments.name: Node Type Id
arguments.description:
This field encodes, through a single value, the resources available to each of
the Spark nodes in this cluster. For example, the Spark nodes can be provisioned
and optimized for memory or compute intensive workloads. A list of available node
types can be retrieved by using the :method:clusters/listNodeTypes API call.

arguments.name: Num Workers
arguments.description:
Number of worker nodes that this cluster should have. A cluster has one Spark Driver
and `num_workers` Executors for a total of `num_workers` + 1 Spark nodes.

Note: When reading the properties of a cluster, this field reflects the desired number
of workers rather than the actual current number of workers. For instance, if a cluster
is resized from 5 to 10 workers, this field will immediately be updated to reflect

increase from 5 to 10 as the new nodes are provisioned.

arguments.name: Single User Name

arguments.name: Spark Conf

Users can also pass in a string of extra JVM options to the driver and the executors via
`spark.driver.extraJavaOptions` and `spark.executor.extraJavaOptions` respectively.

them to `$SPARK_DAEMON_JAVA_OPTS` as shown in the example below. This ensures that all
default databricks managed environmental variables are included as well.

`{"SPARK_DAEMON_JAVA_OPTS": "$SPARK_DAEMON_JAVA_OPTS -Dspark.shuffle.service.enabled=true"}`

arguments.description:

* `EDITABLE`: The job is in an editable state and can be modified.

arguments.description:
A list of task execution environment specifications that can be referenced by serverless tasks of this job.
For serverless notebook tasks, if the environment_key is not specified, the notebook environment will be used if present. If a jobs environment is specified, it will override the notebook environment.
For other serverless tasks, the task environment is required to be specified using environment_key in the task settings.

setupGuide.title: Create Datadog API and application keys
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Use the Datadog US5 site (us5.datadoghq.com). This connection needs one API key and one application key.

steps.title: Create an API key
steps.description: In Datadog, go to Organization Settings > API keys, click New Key, enter a name, and create the key.

steps.title: Create an application key
steps.description: Go to Organization Settings > Application Keys, click New Key, and save the application key secret immediately because Datadog only shows it once.

steps.title: Scope the application key if your organization uses scoped keys
steps.description: Grant the minimum scopes needed for this wrapper: monitors_read, monitors_write, dashboards_read, dashboards_write, monitors_downtime, metrics_read, timeseries_query, events_read, slos_read, and notebooks_read.

steps.title: Enter both keys in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the Datadog API key into the API Key field and the Datadog application key into the Application Key field when creating the connection in MindCloud.

name: DatoCMS
description: Manage content models, publish assets, localize content, and ship updates.

setupGuide.title: Create a DatoCMS API token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: MindCloud uses a DatoCMS API token. New DatoCMS projects only create a default read-only token automatically, so if you need write access you must create a custom token with the right permissions.

steps.title: Open API Tokens in your DatoCMS project
steps.description: Sign in to your DatoCMS project admin area and go to Project Settings > API Tokens.

steps.title: Choose the right token type
steps.description: If you only need read access, you can use the existing read-only token. If MindCloud needs to create, update, or delete content, create a custom API token and assign a role with the required Content Management API permissions.

steps.title: Create or copy the token
steps.description: If you are creating a custom token, name it, assign the correct role, and create it. Then copy the token value and store it securely.

steps.title: Paste the token into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to the MindCloud DatoCMS connection form and paste the copied token into the API key field.

setupGuide.title: Connect Deel with an API token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Open Deel in a browser. This connection uses a Deel API token, and an Organization Token is usually the right choice for the contract, timesheet, milestone, adjustment, and invoice-adjustment actions in this wrapper.

steps.title: Generate a new token
steps.description: Click Generate new token, choose Organization Token unless you specifically need a user-limited personal token, then continue through the token wizard.

steps.title: Select the required scopes and generate the token
steps.description: Choose the scopes your Deel workflows need, review the token settings, and generate the token. Deel only shows the token value once.

steps.title: Paste the token into the connection form
steps.description: Copy the generated token and paste it into the API Token field in the connection form right away.

name: Deskpro
description: Deskpro is a help desk and customer support platform for tickets, users, organizations, knowledge content, and agent workflows.

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow for Deskpro API access.

credentials.name: Helpdesk URL
credentials.description: Full Deskpro helpdesk root URL without a trailing slash, for example https://your-helpdesk.deskpro.com

credentials.name: Auth Endpoint
credentials.description: Full Deskpro OAuth authorization endpoint copied from Deskpro Admin -> Apps -> OAuth -> your client details. Example pattern from Deskpro docs: https://your-helpdesk.example/api/v2/oauth/agent/<clientRecordId>

credentials.name: Token Endpoint
credentials.description: Full Deskpro OAuth token endpoint copied from Deskpro Admin -> Apps -> OAuth -> your client details. Deskpro's official OAuth screenshot shows a token endpoint ending in /api/v2/oauth/token.

setupGuide.title: Connect Deskpro OAuth2
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Deskpro helpdesk URL and a Deskpro OAuth client with authorization code flow enabled.

steps.title: Open Deskpro OAuth settings
steps.description: In Deskpro, go to Admin -> Apps & Integrations -> OAuth and open the OAuth client you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Copy the tenant-specific OAuth details
steps.description: Copy the Helpdesk URL root, Auth endpoint, Token endpoint, Client ID, and Client Secret from the OAuth client details screen.

steps.title: Confirm the redirect URL
steps.description: Make sure the Deskpro OAuth client allows the MindCloud redirect URL https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/deskPro/callback.

steps.title: Enter the helpdesk URL in MindCloud
steps.description: Set Helpdesk URL to your Deskpro root URL without a trailing slash, for example https://your-helpdesk.deskpro.com.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Deskpro API key authentication using the Authorization header format required by Deskpro.

steps.title: Use the Deskpro root URL

steps.title: Create or copy an API key in Deskpro
steps.description: In Deskpro Admin, generate or copy an API key for the account you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Enter the API key in MindCloud

name: Devin
description: AI software engineering agent for creating and managing Devin sessions, knowledge, playbooks, secrets, schedules, and organization resources through the Devin API.

authentication.name: Service User API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate to Devin with a service user API key. Devin v3 API requests use an Authorization bearer token.
authentication.notes: Use a Devin service-user API key with the `Authorization: Bearer {{credentials.apiKey}}` header. Devin service-user credentials are documented with the `cog_` prefix. Do not use a MindCloud `apk_user...` API key here; Devin will reject it with HTTP 403. Organization actions require `org_id` unless an action explicitly works across the enterprise scope.

setupGuide.title: Connect Devin
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to a Devin organization and permission to create or use a service user API key.

steps.title: Open Devin settings
steps.description: Sign in to Devin and open your organization settings.

steps.title: Create or choose a service user
steps.description: Use a service user for API access so requests are auditable and controlled by role-based permissions.

steps.title: Generate an API key
steps.description: Create a service user API key and copy the token value. Devin service user credentials use the cog_ prefix.

steps.title: Find your organization ID
steps.description: Use the organization ID from Devin settings or from Devin API examples for your organization. Many actions require org_id.

setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a DigiSigner account. DigiSigner issues a personal API key in your account settings.

steps.title: Copy your API key

steps.title: Create the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Paste the API key into the API Key field. MindCloud will send it using DigiSigner's documented Basic Auth header format.

name: Digital Samba
description: Digital Samba Embedded provides video conferencing rooms, sessions, participants, recordings, roles, libraries, live usage, statistics, and webhooks through REST APIs.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate Digital Samba REST API requests with a developer key sent as a bearer token.
authentication.notes: Digital Samba REST docs show bearer developer-key authentication. Use the implicit `credentials.apiKey` value; do not create a visible API-key auth argument.

setupGuide.title: Connect Digital Samba
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to a Digital Samba team dashboard with permission to view API developer credentials.

steps.title: Open the Digital Samba dashboard
steps.description: Sign in to the Digital Samba dashboard for the team you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Find the API developer key
steps.description: Use the Digital Samba API authentication guide to locate the developer key for your team. Digital Samba documents this credential as the developer key used for REST API authentication.

steps.title: Paste the key in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the developer key into the API Key field for this connection. Do not add the word Bearer; MindCloud adds the bearer authorization header automatically.

arguments.name: Privacy
arguments.description: Public rooms can be joined using a room link. Private rooms require the room link to include a valid token. Must be in ['public', 'private'].

arguments.description: Select a subset of roles for this room. The order in which they’re added will be the order in which they appear in the Participants panel. Must be an array of role IDs or names.

arguments.description: Must be at least 3 characters. Must not be greater than 500 characters.

arguments.name: External ID
arguments.description: Assign the room with an ID for integration on your side.

arguments.name: Default Role
arguments.description: Select a role to be assigned to participants who join with no token (shared link to public room) or with a token without a role. Role ID or name.

arguments.name: Tags
arguments.description: Must be an array of room tags.

arguments.name: Is Locked
arguments.description: Locked rooms require acceptance to join. Single-role rooms cannot be locked on join.

arguments.name: Topbar Enabled
arguments.description: Set the room with or without a top bar.

arguments.name: Toolbar Enabled
arguments.description: Set the room with or without a toolbar.

arguments.name: Toolbar Position
arguments.description: Choose your desired position for the toolbar for desktop devices. Must be one of left, right or bottom.

arguments.name: Toolbar Color
arguments.description: Select a background colour for the toolbar in this room. Must be color hex code.

arguments.name: Primary Color
arguments.description: Select a colour for buttons and other interactive elements in this room. Must be color hex code.

arguments.name: Background Color
arguments.description: Select a colour for the background in this room. Must be color hex code.

arguments.name: Palette Mode
arguments.description: Palette mode (Appearance) will control the background colour of panels, modals and join screen. Must be one of light or dark.

arguments.name: Language
arguments.description: Select a default language for the room’s UI. Must be one of ar-SA, en, es-ES, de-DE, it-IT, nl-NL, pt-PT, ro-RO, zh-CN or zh-TW.

arguments.name: Audio On Join Enabled
arguments.description: When disabled, users will join the session with muted microphones.

arguments.name: Video On Join Enabled
arguments.description: When disabled, users will join the session with turned-off cameras.

arguments.name: Screenshare Enabled
arguments.description: Allow your participants to share their screen. Mobile users will not be able to share their screen.

arguments.description: When enabled, your participants will have access to the Participants panel.

arguments.name: Logo Enabled

arguments.description: Set rooms with or without a toolbar.

arguments.description: Select a colour for the background in rooms. Must be color hex code.

name: Discord
description: Chat, call, stream, and build communities across Discord servers.

authentication.name: OAuth2 (User Token)
authentication.description: Discord OAuth2 user authorization flow (Bearer token). Use for user-scoped endpoints.

setupGuide.title: Authorize Discord with OAuth2
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Start the Discord connection from MindCloud. Discord will open an authorization page where you sign in and review the scopes requested by the application.

steps.title: Sign in to Discord if prompted
steps.description: When Discord opens the authorization screen, sign in with the Discord account you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Review the requested scopes and server access
steps.description: Check the requested Discord scopes and, if Discord asks for a server selection, choose the correct server for the integration.

steps.title: Approve the connection
steps.description: Authorize the application in Discord to finish the OAuth2 flow.

authentication.name: Bot Token
authentication.description: Use the single API Key field to paste your Discord Bot Token (without the "Bot " prefix). MindCloud sends Authorization: Bot <token>.

setupGuide.title: Create a Discord bot token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: This auth path uses a Discord bot token from a Discord application you control. Bot tokens are highly sensitive and Discord only shows the full token when you reset or create it.

steps.title: Open your application in the Discord Developer Portal
steps.description: Go to the Discord Developer Portal, create a new application if needed, and open the application you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Open the Bot settings
steps.description: In the left sidebar of the application settings, open the Bot page.

steps.title: Create or reset the bot token
steps.description: Use the token controls on the Bot page to create or reset the token, then copy it immediately and store it securely.

steps.title: Paste the bot token into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to the MindCloud Discord connection form and paste the copied token into the Bot Token field.

name: DocumentPro
description: DocumentPro extracts structured data from documents and manages extraction workflows over the DocumentPro REST API.

authentication.name: DocumentPro API Key
authentication.description: Use your DocumentPro API key. DocumentPro requires the key in the x-api-key header on every API request.
authentication.notes: DocumentPro authenticates with a single API key sent as the `x-api-key` request header. Use the same key for the test connection and app agent connection.

credentials.name: API Key
credentials.description: Your DocumentPro API key from the account settings page.

setupGuide.title: Connect DocumentPro
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a DocumentPro workspace API key with access to the workflows and documents you want to manage.

steps.title: Open DocumentPro
steps.description: Sign in to your DocumentPro workspace.

steps.title: Create or copy an API key
steps.description: Open the API key settings in your workspace and copy an active key.

steps.title: Paste the API key here
steps.description: Store that key in the MindCloud connection as the single `API Key` secret.

steps.title: Verify workflow access
steps.description: Confirm the same key can access your target workflow and import email address before saving the connection.

authentication.notes: OpenText Developer Cloud documents OAuth2 token endpoints by region and organization or tenant ID. Classic Documentum D2FS deployments may instead use instance-specific OTDS OAuth2 endpoints; set oauthTokenUrl to the exact endpoint for the target deployment.

credentials.name: Documentum REST base URL
credentials.description: Base URL for the target Documentum REST/D2FS service, for example https://host.example.com/d2fs-rest or https://host.example.com/dctm-rest.

credentials.name: OAuth token URL
credentials.description: Exact OpenText/OTDS OAuth2 token endpoint for this deployment.

credentials.name: Client ID
credentials.description: Confidential OAuth client ID for the OpenText application.

credentials.name: Client secret
credentials.description: Confidential OAuth client secret for the OpenText application.

setupGuide.title: Connect OpenText Documentum
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Have the target Documentum REST or D2FS base URL, the exact OAuth2 token endpoint for the deployment, and a confidential OpenText OAuth client ID and secret.

steps.title: Confirm the Documentum REST base URL
steps.description: Use the deployment URL for Documentum REST or D2FS. OpenText Documentum D2FS examples use instance-hosted paths such as /d2fs-rest or /dctm-rest before /repositories.

steps.title: Confirm the OAuth token endpoint
steps.description: For OpenText Developer Cloud, token endpoints are region and tenant or organization specific. For classic Documentum deployments, use the OTDS token endpoint configured for that instance.

steps.title: Enter the confidential OAuth client credentials
steps.description: Use the Confidential Client ID and Client Secret from the OpenText application. Do not use the public client for server-side token exchange.

steps.title: Save and authenticate
steps.description: The connection exchanges the client credentials at the configured token endpoint and sends the resulting bearer token to Documentum REST actions.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Connect with a Documo API key generated from the Documo app.

setupGuide.title: Create a Documo API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Documo Business plan or higher and the API Add-On purchased for the account.

steps.title: Purchase the API Add-On
steps.description: In the Documo app, open the billing section and purchase the API Add-On for your account. Documo states that this add-on requires a Business plan or higher.

steps.title: Open API Keys
steps.description: In the Documo app, open the Toolbox menu and select API Keys.

steps.title: Create a new key
steps.description: Click Create and complete the form. You can check the option to have the key emailed to you if you want a copy sent by email.

steps.title: Store the key securely
steps.description: Copy the API key immediately or use the emailed copy. Documo says you will not be able to view the secret again after creation.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate with a DocuPanda API key sent in the shared X-API-Key header on every request.
authentication.notes: DocuPanda's OpenAPI security scheme requires the exact request header X-API-Key. Do not use native MindCloud apiKey auth because runtime bearer injection would violate the provider contract.

credentials.name: API Key
credentials.description: Your DocuPanda API key used in the X-API-Key header.

setupGuide.title: Set up your DocuPanda API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Generate an API key in your DocuPanda workspace, then paste it into MindCloud using the API Key field.

steps.title: Open DocuPanda API settings
steps.description: In DocuPanda, open your workspace settings and navigate to the API key management page.

steps.title: Create or copy an API key
steps.description: Create a new API key if needed, or copy an existing key that has access to the workspace you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to MindCloud and paste the value into the API Key field, then save and test the connection.

An exact copy of the original standardization JSON object, except every value is replaced with a dictionary with the following values:
- **value**: The original value
- **review**:
   - **page**: The page number on which the value was found

name: Dotcom Monitor

authentication.description: Authenticates against the Dotcom-Monitor Web API by exchanging a Monitoring Web API UID for a cookie-backed session.

steps.title: Allow API access from MindCloud

steps.title: Paste the Web API UID into MindCloud
steps.description: Use the Web API UID as the only credential field for this connection. MindCloud will use it to call POST /login and store the returned session cookies automatically.

name: Doyle HCM
description: Doyle HCM provides payroll and HR services for U.S. employers through white-label employer and employee payroll portals backed by Worklio.

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: Doyle HCM uses Worklio direct-mode OAuth 2.0 Resource Owner flow for server-to-server API access.
authentication.notes: Use the existing Worklio developer account for the Doyle HCM white-label deployment. Authentication uses only username and password at connection time; MindCloud exchanges them for a bearer token at https://api.worklio.com/connect/token with scope api. Partner ID is stored with the credential source for later reference but is not part of the token request.

setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Doyle HCM uses Worklio direct mode OAuth 2.0 Resource Owner flow. MindCloud exchanges your Worklio developer-account username and password for a bearer token at https://api.worklio.com/connect/token using the documented scope api.

steps.title: Open the Doyle employer payroll login
steps.description: Go to https://doylehcm.worklio.com and sign in with the existing Worklio developer account you want MindCloud to use for Doyle HCM.

steps.title: Confirm the account works on Doyle HCM
steps.description: After sign-in, make sure you can reach the Doyle HCM payroll dashboard. This confirms the username and password are valid for the Doyle white-label deployment.

steps.title: Create the MindCloud test connection
steps.description: In the Doyle HCM connection form, enter the same username and password. MindCloud already uses the documented direct-mode client ID, client secret, and scope.

steps.title: Verify the connection
steps.description: Run the test connection. A successful test proves MindCloud can call GET /wep/me with the generated bearer token.

authentication.description: Connect Dubsado with a Zapier API key for /zapier/key validation plus live browser request-header values for session-backed web-app actions. Session-backed actions use Cookie, XCSRF Token, and XBrand from the Request Headers section of a logged-in app.dubsado.com API request.

credentials.name: API Key
credentials.description: Zapier API key generated from Dubsado Integrations.

credentials.name: Cookie
credentials.description: Full Cookie value copied from the Request Headers section of an authenticated app.dubsado.com API request.

credentials.name: XCSRF Token
credentials.description: x-csrf-token value copied from the Request Headers section of the same authenticated app.dubsado.com API request.

credentials.name: XBrand
credentials.description: x-brand value copied from the Request Headers section of the same authenticated app.dubsado.com API request.

setupGuide.title: Connect Dubsado
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Use the Dubsado account tied to the provided Zapier API key. Retrieve the API key from 1Password unless it has been rotated.

steps.title: Generate or confirm the Zapier token
steps.description: In Dubsado, go to Settings > Integrations > Zapier and copy the current API key.

steps.title: Paste the API key into MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the Dubsado API key into the API Key field.

steps.title: Open a logged-in API request
steps.description: In your browser, open app.dubsado.com, sign in, open DevTools, go to Network, click a successful API request, and open its Request Headers section.

steps.title: Copy the Cookie header
steps.description: From Request Headers, copy the Cookie header value into the Cookie field.

steps.title: Copy the x-csrf-token header
steps.description: From the same Request Headers section, copy the x-csrf-token value into the XCSRF Token field.

steps.title: Copy the x-brand header
steps.description: From the same Request Headers section, copy the x-brand value into the XBrand field.

steps.title: Save and test the connection
steps.description: Save the connection. The built-in test verifies the API key path immediately, and the session-backed actions will use the additional Cookie, XCSRF Token, and XBrand values.

steps.title: Paste the token into the connection
steps.description: Return to MindCloud and paste the copied Dynosend token into the API key field for this connection.
